subject: general
question: A is 6 years older than B. 10 years ago, B's age was three quarters of A's age. Find the present age (in years) of A.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **age difference** (6 years) always remains constant.

10 years ago, ratio of B : A = 3 : 4.

Difference in ratio units = 4 − 3 = 1 unit → 6 years.

A's age 10 years ago = 4 units = 4 × 6 = 24 years.

A's present age = 24 + 10 = 34 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 34 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present age of A = **A**

Present age of B = **B**

A = B + 6 ⇒ B = A − 6

**Formula Used:**

Age 10 years ago = (Present Age − 10)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5656081c15335b48ecdd8994bb0f7ea5bf8eccc786f046c2b9f362617efb35e9.png] 

**Calculations:**

According to the question, 10 years ago:

⇒ B − 10 = 3/4 × (A − 10)

Substitute B = A − 6:

⇒ (A − 6) − 10 = 3/4 × (A − 10)

⇒ A − 16 = 3/4 × (A − 10)

⇒ 4 × (A − 16) = 3 × (A − 10)

⇒ 4A − 64 = 3A − 30

⇒ 4A − 3A = 64 − 30

⇒ A = 34

**∴ The correct answer is 34 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two people remains the **same** throughout their lives, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages at time t₁ is x:y and the difference is D, then 1 unit of ratio = D ÷ |x−y|.

Linear Equation Method

For age problems involving multiple time periods, always define variables based on **present ages** to avoid confusion during calculation.</p
